seo_title: Cost of Living in Valencia 2026: Visa, Prices, Reviews | Relocost
seo_description: How much does it cost to live in Valencia per month, do Russians need a visa, work, rent and reviews from those who relocated. A realistic moving budget in the Relocost calculator.
intro_text: A Mediterranean alternative to Barcelona: 30% cheaper, the same climate and a more relaxed pace. Popular for relocation among freelancers via the digital nomad visa and families with children.
pros: The Mediterranean, mild winters and over 300 sunny days a year
Prices 30% lower than Barcelona with the same climate
A digital nomad visa for remote workers and a 24% tax regime
Good international schools and developed private healthcare
Turia Park — 9 km of cycle paths running across the whole city
cons: Hot summers of +35°C and high humidity off the sea
Weaker business infrastructure than Madrid and Barcelona
Rents are rising due to the influx of digital nomads

visa_steps.title: Schengen visa or residence permit
visa_steps.description: For a long stay — a national D visa with an appointment at the consulate.

visa_steps.title: Digital Nomad Visa
visa_steps.description: For remote workers earning from €2,763 a month. A 1-year residence permit, extendable up to 5 years.

visa_steps.title: NIE and TIE
visa_steps.description: An identification number and a physical resident card. You can book an appointment about a month out.

visa_steps.title: Empadronamiento
visa_steps.description: Registration at your address with the Ayuntamiento. Needed for school, healthcare and a bank.

visa_steps.title: Bank account
visa_steps.description: Sabadell, BBVA and CaixaBank work with residents. The online bank N26 suits digital nomads.

faq.question: How is Valencia different from Barcelona?
faq.answer: Smaller, calmer and cheaper. Fewer tourists and easier to arrange a rental.

faq.question: How is the language situation in Valencia?
faq.answer: Spanish is essential for daily life, English works in tourism and IT. The Valencian dialect comes up but isn't critical.

faq.question: Which districts are good for families in Valencia?
faq.answer: Benimaclet — student and family-friendly. Campanar — modern. L'Alqueria — outskirts with villas.

faq.question: Should I learn the language before moving to Valencia?
faq.answer: Yes, at least A2 — otherwise you'll struggle with public services, school and healthcare.

faq.question: Where is the sea in Valencia?
faq.answer: Malvarrosa and Las Arenas beaches are 15 minutes by tram from the centre. Perfect in summer.

faq.question: How is the internet in Valencia?
faq.answer: Fibre at 600+ Mbps for €30. 4G everywhere. Excellent infrastructure for remote work.

reviews.text: We got the DNV for the whole family and rent an apartment in Ruzafa for €1,200. My daughter is at an international school and I work for a US company. Valencia is a balance of climate, price and Europe.
I moved from Tbilisi: Schengen, the sea, and I'm learning the language from scratch. Rent is expensive, but the cafés and Turia Park make up for it.
